abeo: ăb-ĕo, ĭvi or ii, ītum, īre
abscondo: abs-condo, condi and condĭdi, condĭtum and consum, 3
adeo: ăd-ĕo, ĭī, and rarely īvi, ĭtum, 4
amor: ămor, like honos, labos, colos, ōris, m.
anguis: anguis, is, like sanguen for sanguis
apollo: ăpollo, ĭnis, like hemo for homo
aspicio: a-spĭcĭo, others except Halm, spexi, spectum, 3
bos: bōs, bŏvis, like bovare for boare
cauda: cauda, like codex, plostrum, ae, f.
cieo: cĭĕo, cīvi, cĭtum, 2, cīre, prevailing in the compounds accio, excio
clamor: clāmor, like arbos, labos, ōris, m.
color: cŏlor, like arbos, clamos, honos, ōris, m.
dumosus: dūmōsus, like Casmena, Casmili, a, um
ineo: ĭn-ĕo, īvi and ĭi, ĭtum, īre
lauo: lăvo, lāvi, lautum, lăvātum and lōtum
minerua: Mĭnerva, like magester, leber, ae, f.
munio: munĭo, ōnis, a false reading for nomionem
o: O, the fourteenth letter of the Latin alphabet
odor: ŏdor, like arbos, labos, ōris, m.
olus: Olus, i, another form for Aulus
percurro: per-curro, percŭcurri or percurri, percursum, 3, n.
poto: pōto, āvi, ātum, or pōtum, 1, n.
praesaepe: praesaepe, is, ae, ii, n., f.
pudeo: pŭdĕo, ŭi, or pŭdĭtum est, ēre
tendo: tendo, tĕtendi, tentum and tensum, 3, n.
terminus: termĭnus, i, ōnis, ĭnis, m., n.
tiberis: Tĭbĕris, is, is or ĭdis, m.
transeo: trans-ĕo, īvi or ĭi, ĭtum, īre
tundo: tundo, tŭtŭdi, tunsum, tūssum, and tusum
